title: Window Rebates in Los Angeles 2026: $2.00 per Sq Ft from LADWP | HomePowerRebate
desc: LADWP pays $2.00 per square foot for ENERGY STAR windows with U-factor 0.30 or lower and SHGC 0.25 or lower. Skylights, permit rules, exclusions and steps.
lead: LADWP pays $2.00 per square foot of ENERGY STAR window, and it sets firm performance numbers a window has to meet. It is one of the few Los Angeles-area utilities that rebates windows at all.
cards_intro: These figures come from LADWP's Consumer Rebate Program page, which we read on October 2, 2026. New construction, additions and ADUs are not eligible, and you need a final approved Building and Safety permit.

cards.title: Windows and glass doors
cards.note: U-factor of 0.30 or lower and SHGC of 0.25 or lower.

cards.title: Skylights
cards.note: U-factor of 0.50 or lower and SHGC of 0.28 or lower.

cards.title: Proof
cards.note: A manufacturer's sheet that lists the U-factor, SHGC and dimensions of each window, or the NFRC label.

after_cards:
A worked example

Replacing 150 square feet of window glass earns 150 x $2.00 = $300. A whole-house job of 300 square feet earns $600. That is a small share of the cost of new windows, so treat the rebate as a bonus and choose windows for comfort and noise, not for the rebate.
sections: Read the two numbers on the label

The U-factor measures how well a window holds in heat, and the solar heat gain coefficient (SHGC) measures how much sun energy gets through. LADWP's limits of 0.30 and 0.25 are tight, and they match the cooling focus of its program. A window with a low SHGC blocks more solar heat, which helps in a hot summer. Ask for the National Fenestration Rating Council label for each window and check both numbers against LADWP's before you order.
What LADWP asks you to send

A paid itemized invoice with the quantity of windows and their dimensions, the manufacturer's order confirmation sheet or the NFRC label, and a final approved permit from the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety. Applications go in online through your LADWP account or by mail within 12 months of purchase, and LADWP can inspect the installation before it pays.

LADWP is the only utility we checked in this part of Los Angeles County whose rebate list names windows. Pasadena, Burbank and Glendale do not list a window rebate that we could read. Los Angeles's average January low over 2015 to 2024 was 7.9°C, so a window's value here comes from summer heat and noise, not winter cold.

Insulation and air sealing usually pay back faster than windows, and LADWP pays $0.50 to $0.75 per square foot for attic insulation (see Los Angeles attic insulation rebates). If your budget is limited, do the attic first and the windows later. The federal 25C and 25D tax credits ended for spending after December 31, 2025.
What to ask the window installer

Ask for the NFRC label numbers in writing for every window, since a mixed order can include one that misses LADWP's limits. Ask whether the quote covers trim, stucco or siding repair, and disposal. Ask who pulls the LADBS permit and who schedules the inspection, because LADWP will not pay without the final approved permit. If your windows face a busy street, ask about the sound rating as well. A good window cuts noise as well as heat, and that is often the reason Los Angeles homeowners replace them.
claim_heading: How to claim the LADWP rebate
claim_steps: Check that LADWP is your electric utility and that the home is not new construction, an addition or an ADU.
Choose windows with a U-factor of 0.30 or lower and an SHGC of 0.25 or lower, and keep the NFRC labels.
Have the windows installed under a Building and Safety permit and get the permit finaled.
Collect the paid invoice with quantities and dimensions, plus the order sheet or label.
Apply through your LADWP account or by mail within 12 months of purchase.
LADWP may inspect before it sends the rebate check.
faq: How much does LADWP pay for windows?
$2.00 per square foot of qualifying ENERGY STAR window.
What performance numbers do I need?
For windows and glass doors, a U-factor of 0.30 or lower and an SHGC of 0.25 or lower. For skylights, 0.50 or lower and 0.28 or lower.
No. New construction, additions and accessory dwelling units are excluded.
Yes, a final approved Building and Safety permit.
Should I replace windows or add insulation first?
Insulation usually pays back faster. LADWP pays $0.50 to $0.75 per square foot for attic insulation.
